Review scope: complete extracted claim, the single TODO implementation association and complete annotated TODO test in crates/sage-meta/tests/service_spec.rs, plus captured crate-model context and review rules. This is an accepted explicit deferral, not verification of implemented language restriction handling.

The claim requires (1) restrictions to be explicit at their semantic boundary; (2) each intentionally excluded construct to state its exclusion, rationale, user-visible impact and responsible phase response; (3) the usual response to be a diagnostic or conservative incomplete result; and (4) any temporary semantic approximation, including the example Lifetime::Dummy, to be explicitly identified as a soundness exception rather than full Rust semantics. The sole implementation entry is inside sage_meta::todo and expressly says uniform restriction/completeness accounting is not enforced at every semantic boundary. That gap encompasses the universal boundary requirement and the required information/response accounting; it does not assert that a particular runtime mechanism already fulfills any of these obligations. No ordinary or N/A implementation entry exists to assess.

The sole test, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_explicit_restrictions, has an empty executable body and TODO status. Its comment describes the missing per-restriction acceptance/rejection fixtures and comparison of observable diagnostic, incomplete result or documented approximation against stated impact. It has no assertions and therefore proves none of the claim, including exception labeling. The prerequisite is the explicitly missing uniform boundary restriction/completeness accounting together with a restriction inventory specifying exclusion, rationale, impact, phase response and any soundness exception; focused fixtures must then exercise each restriction at its owning phase and assert the advertised outcomes. The adjacent implementation TODO and this test comment adequately expose the deferred scope rather than misrepresenting this empty test as coverage. In particular, silent approximation or a missing rationale would not currently be caught; these remain part of the admitted gap.

No production helper is supplied or relied upon for this deferred association, and no additional implementation association is necessary to justify the deferral. Captured model context distinguishes this rule from temporary supported-feature gaps and downstream completeness guarantees; approval here does not resolve those separate anchors. Commands executed were cargo meta review start and review read to capture the sources and governing review/Rust guidelines, followed by review record. No behavioral test or workspace build was run by this reviewer, and no code was changed. The result accepts the accuracy of the visible TODO evidence only; all functional guarantees remain deferred.
